text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- German insurance company Allianz buys back 34 pct in Allianz Via Holding France from Compagnie de Navigation Mixte, a subsidiary of Paribas, for 2.2 billion francs.
-- Chairman of French employers' federation CNPF labour committee says youth internship programs should be part of a higher education curriculum.
-- Government postpones reforming status of nickel mining group Eramet but considers replacing chairman Yves Rambaud.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Consumer spending rose 3.1 percent in 1996, but was sluggish in the last quarter of 1996.

-- Lyonnaise des Eaux to take legal action against the government in connection with water pollution linked to intensive farming in Brittany, after company was sued by clients over the poor quality of the water supplied.

-- Lagardere Groupe said it would consider taking part in privatisation of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF implemented through a combination of private placements and public share offering "on the condition that the latter remains marginal". Government expected to decide on method of privatisation soon.
L'AGEFI
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis chaired opening session of the National Committee of the Euro yesterday.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- France Telecom chairman Michel Bon says he expects partial listing on the Paris bourse to draw over 25 billion francs.
-- Foreign groups buy French firms to gain access to the French market rather than increase their industrial capacity, study shows.
-- Government considers a multi-year order of 48 Rafale fighter aircraft from Dassault Aviation.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Unions in transport sector call for 24-hour strike today for drivers to demand early retirement at 55 and a 35-hour work week.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Dassault Aviation offered French state a 10 percent discount from asking price of 300 million francs for each Rafale plane.
